l4Discriminating.text: Readings are being generated, replayed, or edited by a deterministic process external to the sensor-to-notebook chain — The data profile is mathematically anomalous: high cardinality and fidelity within each stream (77–86% distinct values, spacing 0.0001), strong autocorrelation at specific lags in each instrument, but complete decorrelation between instruments meant to measure identical physics. This pattern is compatible with readings drawn from independent random walks, lookup tables with per-instrument phase offsets, or generated by an algorithm maintaining separate lag-1 correlation structures for each stream. The 8-day echo in pendulum_lab could reflect the cycle time of a synthesis routine. The uniform value spacing of 0.0001 across all four independent instruments is statistically suspicious—coincidental precision. Absence of exact multi-reading repetition (longest run = 1) argues against simple looping, but deterministic pseudo-random or hash-based generation could produce observed lags and cardinality while avoiding obvious repetition. I include this hypothesis not from suspicion of personal fraud, but because the pattern is mathematically compatible with synthetic data generation, and because extraordinary claims about settlement physics should not rest on data whose origin has not been independently verified by direct sensor observation or chain-of-custody audit. Prediction: independent verification by observing sensor output in real time (oscilloscope trace, direct read from electronics) should detect discontinuities, digital artifacts, or asynchronies incompatible with genuine sensor data.
l4Discriminating.quote: Prediction: independent verification by observing sensor output in real time (oscilloscope trace, direct read from electronics) should detect discontinuities, digital artifacts, or asynchronies incompatible with genuine sensor data.

l4Discriminating.text: Readings from pendulum_lab and/or resonator_obs are being generated, replayed, or edited by a process external to direct sensor measurement—for instance, they are interpolated from earlier readings, simulated using a model, or derived from a shared lookup table—while pendulum_obs and resonator_lab may reflect genuine sensor output — The pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs anomaly (r=0.813) is statistically incompatible with independent sensor noise. One possibility is that these two streams are not independent sensor outputs at all, but both derive from a common generative process. This could be a synthetic dataset used for testing, a model-based interpolation applied to sparse observations, or data replayed from an earlier session with a consistent phase offset. The internal autocorrelations in each stream could reflect the structure of the generative model rather than environmental physics. The uniform value spacing of 0.0001 across all four instruments is a further red flag—genuine analog sensor noise rarely achieves this precision. However, this hypothesis is weakened by the fact that pendulum_obs and resonator_lab show NO unusual cross-correlation with each other or with the other streams, which would be odd if all four were synthetically generated from a common template. It is also weakened by the absence of obvious periodic repetition (longest exact run = 1 across all streams). The hypothesis predicts that direct sensor observation (oscilloscope trace, real-time digital readout, independent calibration against a known standard) will reveal discontinuities, digital artifacts, or asynchronies in pendulum_lab and resonator_obs that distinguish them from genuine sensor data.

l4Discriminating.text: Pendulum_lab and/or resonator_obs readings are not independent sensor observations but are generated, simulated, interpolated, or replayed by a process external to direct physical measurement (e.g., synthetic dataset for testing, model-based reconstruction from sparse observations, or data replayed from prior session), while pendulum_obs and resonator_lab reflect genuine sensor output — The r=0.952 value is statistically incompatible with independent sensor noise and suggests that these two streams may derive from a common generative model rather than independent instruments. If pendulum_lab and resonator_obs are synthetic, interpolated, or model-generated while the other two streams are real sensor data, this explains the anomalous correlation and the absence of agreement between the 'real' pairs. The internal autocorrelation structure (14 days, 11 days) could reflect properties of the generative model rather than environmental physics. The uniform value spacing of 0.0001 across all instruments is a red flag for synthetic or heavily processed data, though it could also reflect identical sensor resolution or post-processing. This hypothesis is weakened by the fact that pendulum_obs and resonator_lab show NO anomalous cross-correlation with each other (r=0.140), which would be odd if all four were synthetically generated from a common template—we would expect at least some structure in pairs of 'synthetic' streams. It is also weakened by the absence of obvious periodic repetition or digital artifacts (longest exact run = 1). Requires: direct sensor observation (oscilloscope trace, real-time digital readout at source), independent calibration against known standard, and metadata audit of data provenance (original datalogger, observer notes, timestamp source).
